text:
emma.sales: Orenda POC in eu-central: after switching to redwood/q5a_kv the demo team reported huge lag. First-token spiking to ~1.2s and intermittent 429s. Can we swarm? They're on a scheduled demo in 3 hours.

theo.eng: Which endpoint and model rollout did you flip? Any sample requests or headers?

emma.sales: Using /v1/chat/complete, model=redwood/q5a_kv-rc1, routed to dedicated-eu-2. Sample payload: `{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Show me the latest invoice for acct 123"}],"max_tokens":64}`. Headers include `x-customer-id: orenda` and `x-session: orenda-2026-09-12-0152-uid`.

priya.ml: Two quick notes: q5a_kv changes tokenization/kv footprint slightly; but 1.2s TTFT + 429s sounds like both cache churn and rate limiting. Do we have logs showing `kv_cache: evict` or `throttle: 429`?

emma.sales: Debug logs from the customer: `kv_cache: evict key=conv:orenda:session:uid` repeated and `rate_limiter: permit_denied instance=inst-7`. Also saw `serving: batch_size=1 queue_wait=950ms`.

nate.runtime: Oof. On Dedicated we had a low per-instance concurrency cap for that fleet due to a recent rollout (`per_instance_concurrency=8`) and NA/EMEA routing bump caused one pod to get flooded. Also batch_window_ms is at 8 currently which explains many size=1 batches.

theo.eng: How is their session id constructed? Looks like it's including a timestamp which makes every request a new prefix key. That will trash prefix caching.

emma.sales: Yes it's generated client-side with epoch ms. They said it helps them correlate logs.

priya.ml: Ask them to stop embedding epoch in the prompt. Recommend `x-session` header instead and keep prompts stable. Meanwhile we can change runtime: bump `batch_window_ms` to 40ms, raise `per_instance_concurrency` to 32 for dedicated-eu-2, enable `prefetch=true`, and extend `kv_cache_ttl` from 60s -> 300s.

nate.runtime: I can apply those toggles. deploy-bot: config-change requested: target=dedicated-eu-2 params={batch_window_ms:40, per_instance_concurrency:32, prefetch:true, kv_cache_ttl:300} by nate.runtime.

deploy-bot: patching control plane...

deploy-bot: control plane patch applied. workers rolling.

amber.cs: I pushed a quick note to Orenda recommending they remove the epoch from the prompt and use `x-session`. Also offered extra POC credits for the run.

secops-bot: security checklist: SOC2_report=v2025_q4 (available), private_peering=possible via audit, ip_allowlist=dedicated supported. Amber.cs: filing docs share.

deploy-bot: rollout complete for dedicated-eu-2.

nate.runtime: After change, I replayed 200 representative requests. Median TTFT dropped to ~150ms, 95p ~260ms. Rate limiter logs reduced and cache miss rate went from 42% -> 8%.

emma.sales: Customer confirmed demo went fine; mentioned they still see a few slow requests when they run single-shot ad-hoc queries.

priya.ml: That's probably still a combination of occasional unique prefixes and some small-batch fallthrough. Long-term: 1) add onboarding warning when prompts contain high-entropy tokens like epoch timestamps; 2) expose `batch_window_ms` suggestion in Console per-deployment; 3) consider `auto_prefetch` heuristic for Dedicated. Filing ticket ML-3121.

theo.eng: Also recommend we add a small SDK snippet for best practice: put session ids in headers and reuse prompt prefix.

amber.cs: I'll send SOC2 and peering docs and propose a 3-month reserved capacity offer for consistent low-latency.

emma.sales: Thanks all — closing POC blocker. Notes for handoff: share config diff, the recorded run numbers, and follow up on ML-3121.

nate.runtime: Filed infra ticket RUNTIME-4981 to add alerting for per-deployment cache-miss>30% and auto-suggest tuning.

emma.sales: Great, cheers everyone! :party_popper:
